name: Other Professional, Scientific And Technical Activities
notes: Labour (L) = compensation of employees (D1, GBP 10,388m) plus GBP 225m of the industry's mixed income (the self-employed's income): section M's labour share of income (66.8%, uk-labour-share) times mixed income of GBP 336m. Mixed income by section is back-solved (GOS = D1 x (1 / labour share - 1); mixed income = GOS & MI - GOS) and spread over the section's industries pro rata to their gross operating surplus and mixed income. That spread is an assumption (Claude, 2026-10-06). Capital (K) = gross value added - L, so K includes taxes less subsidies on production (GBP 9m).

Energy, materials and services (E, M, S) sort this industry's 2023 intermediate use at purchasers' prices by product: energy = coal, crude oil and gas & metal ores (B06 & B07), refined petroleum, electricity, gas and steam; crude and refined products bought by refining and chemicals, and oil and gas bought by oil and gas extraction, count as materials; all other goods (CPA sections A, B, C) are materials; everything else is services. This is Claude's rule, not an ONS or BEA classification; no UK published E/M/S exists to compare with. Weak spots: B06 & B07 mixes oil and gas with metal ores; D352_3 includes steam and air conditioning; B09 mining support and C33 repair services count as goods.
Capital: stock, investment and depreciation figures are for the wider ONS group M74_75, shared with other industries (see the capital basis note).

Labour figures are ASHE 2023 revised, all employees, gross annual pay (tax year to April 2023, employees in the same job for the whole year; this covers 22,783 thousand jobs against 27,645 thousand in the April pay-period tables). Jobs are rounded to the thousand and are indicative, not headcount. The ASHE wage bill (jobs x mean annual pay) is a sample-based figure that runs well below national-accounts compensation of employees, so the two are not expected to match.

Occupation tables are for the whole SIC section M, not for this industry alone (ASHE Table 29 has sections only): 18 of 26 two-digit occupation groups are published, covering 98% of the section's annual-pay jobs. Withheld cells (CV above 20%, or disclosive) are null, never zero, so occupation totals on the page are lower bounds. Supervisory = SOC 2020 major group 1 (sub-major groups 11 and 12); nonsupervisory = all other sub-major groups.

College / non-college split uses ONS CALI pay shares for the industry group LMN (Real estate activities; Professional, scientific and technical activities; Administrative and support service activities), 2023: degree or higher (qualification levels HQ5 + HQ6) = 58.3% of the group's pay; HQ4 (higher education below degree) counts as non-college. Applied to this industry's L as an assumption that every industry in the group has the group's mix.

Carbon: ONS industry group(s) 74 cover this industry exactly (no apportioning). 2023, residence basis, direct (scope 1) emissions only, IPCC AR5 weights; households' own emissions are not in any industry. Fluorinated gases are the published HFC, PFC, SF6 and NF3 cells ([low] cells are blank in the source, so this can be slightly short).

capital.basis_name: Other professional, scientific and vetinary activities
capital.basis_note: Stocks, investment and depreciation are for ONS industry M74_75 (Other professional, scientific and vetinary activities), a wider group that this industry shares with Vets; the figures are for the whole group, not this industry alone. Investment is ONS GFCF industry "74 to 75", which also covers other UK industries in this viewer. Depreciation published only for CAPSTK industry MC (M73, M74_75); the rate shown is that group's depreciation divided by the group's net stock, and no depreciation amount is shown for this industry.
